reconstructed_theorem_text: For all real numbers g and b satisfying 0 ≤ g, 0 ≤ b, and 0 < g + b, one has b / (g + b) ≤ b + (1 - sqrt(g))² and b + (1 - sqrt(g))² ≤ b + (1 - g)². Here sqrt(g) is the nonnegative real square root of g.
objects: The real numbers g and b; their sum g + b; sqrt(g); and the real-valued expressions b / (g + b), b + (1 - sqrt(g))², and b + (1 - g)².
domains: g and b range over ℝ. All operands, sums, differences, quotients, squares, and inequalities are interpreted in ℝ; each exponent is the natural number 2.
quantifiers: Universal quantification over g and b, written as implicit Lean binders {g b : ℝ}. There are no existential quantifiers.
conclusion: Both b / (g + b) ≤ b + (1 - sqrt(g))² and b + (1 - sqrt(g))² ≤ b + (1 - g)².
scopes: The quantifiers over g and b encompass all three successive hypotheses and the entire conjunction. Each hypothesis applies to both inequalities, which hold for the same g and b. In both right-hand expressions b is added outside the square; each square applies to the entire parenthesized difference. The quotient denominator is the entire sum g + b. Real division is totalized with value zero at denominator zero, but that case is excluded by 0 < g + b. Only the approved nonnegative-input meaning of Real.sqrt is needed because 0 ≤ g.
constant_dependencies: There are no auxiliary constants, free parameters, or existence-chosen quantities. The fixed numerals 0, 1, and 2 are independent of g and b; both inequalities depend only on the universally quantified g and b and the standard real operations and Real.sqrt.
